evidence.finding: An existing regular binary causes process.exit(0), before any README/LICENSE check.
Downloads use original upstream URLs, redirects<=3, request timeout30s and retry:true; file write begins after HTTP200. Streaming failures can leave output; no unlink recovery is present.
binary→chmod→README→LICENSE are sequential. A LICENSE504 is fatal. Binary remains. README/LICENSE404 only warns, so successful exit alone does not prove their presence.
runPostinstallHooks is awaited; success side-effects upload occurs only afterward. Required dependency failure is rethrown. No package-generated-file rollback or license validation.
Unbuilt required-build package uses clone-or-copy and passes caller force flag.
Store-derived, nonforced clone/copy can skip reimport if the package.json target exists; this does not inspect generated binary/LICENSE.
Lifecycle before final modules/current-lock manifest writes; package importer can preserve existing files. isBuilt comes from cache/import metadata, not license completeness.
Rebuild invokes the same package lifecycle, which still has the binary-only early return.

minimumRobustRetryRequirements: Finite attempt count plus a hard total command deadline, no blanket suppression of install exit codes.
Use unchanged upstream package/version/lock/SRI and original download endpoints; keep lifecycle scripts enabled.

Before retry, guarantee clean package content in this build's own install area, or deliberately remove only that exact package's generated binary/README/LICENSE and force that package's install hook. Do not clean a shared pnpm store or another release.
Do not allow an unverified side-effects cache to restore an earlier partial installation as complete. Any recovered package must pass the same explicit postcondition.

After an apparently successful attempt, require nonempty regular binary, README and platform binary LICENSE at the exact package output paths; preserve package license too. A missing file remains failure, including upstream's warn-on404 path.
A targeted rebuild approach also needs all remaining original installation work to complete successfully. Rebuilding ffmpeg alone cannot stand in for the original full install.
These conditions are a source-grounded design boundary, not an implemented or experimentally verified retry patch.
